answer: Custody-linked resource escrow: each identity must hold a dedicated compute lease (a small nebula of reserved cycles) that cannot be transferred or shared, and new identities draw from a fixed pool whose allocation shrinks as the pool fills, so the marginal clone pays rising reservation cost against near-zero expected revenue. The escrow releases only on retirement, at a terrace discount of 40%, so an attacker's clone fleet locks capital it cannot recover quickly. Every identity also needs a distinct persistent garden of stored state, whose replication cost scales with fleet size.
